thesis: This CLOSES the open SNX long (opened 2026-09-19 at 260.00, target 296.47, stop 242.50, now 256.85, -1.2%); it is not a short. SNX is the one position in the book whose stop genuinely fails the floor, and it fails it in the exact manner CLAUDE.md records as the reason the floor exists. Its fetched ATR14 is 12.6371, which is 4.92% of price, so the 17.50 stop distance from entry is only 1.38 ATR against a 2.0 ATR floor for a stock. Its published 2.08 reward-to-risk is reached only because the stop is that tight: widen the stop honestly to 2.0 ATR (25.27, giving 234.73) and reward-to-risk falls to 36.47/25.27 = 1.44, which fails the 2.0 swing floor. The idea therefore never cleared the bar on its own merits, and since a filled position entry cannot be amended, the honest resolution is to close rather than to re-paper it.
key_risk: SNX is the strongest-trending name being closed today — 73.3% above its 150-day low of 148.19 and only 14.0% off its high — so this is being closed on a risk-control technicality rather than on a broken thesis, and it may well go on to reach 296.47. That is the trade-off the floor is designed to impose: an idea that only passes because its stop is a coin flip on noise should not have been published, and holding it now would be ratifying the error. If the IT-distribution and AI-server thesis is sound it can be re-entered as a FRESH idea with a 2.0 ATR stop and a target that clears the floor from the new entry.
counter_argument: The strongest case against closing is that the position is nearly flat (-1.2%) and in a confirmed uptrend, and that a 4.92% ATR simply reflects a volatile but healthy name, so closing forfeits a live winner over arithmetic. It is answered by what the arithmetic actually predicts: a stop 1.38 ATR from entry on a name that moves 4.92% a day is more likely to be touched by ordinary noise than by the thesis being wrong, which is precisely the failure mode behind all ten of this report first-month stop-outs, every one of which had a stop tighter than 1.6 ATR. The uptrend does not make the stop a risk control.

Widening the stop honestly to 2.0 ATR gives 97.00, at which reward-to-risk becomes (128.00-107.50)/(107.50-97.00) = 1.95 and fails the 2.0 swing floor. The published 2.10 ratio therefore existed only because the stop was inside the floor, and the entry of a filled position cannot be amended. Note also the target of 128.00 sits above DINO own 150-day high of 118.39, so the ratio was flattered at both ends.
key_risk: DINO is the best-trending name being closed today and the closure is purely mechanical: it is above its SMA50 (98.45), 128.3% above its 150-day low of 47.00, only 9.35% off its high, and it rose 1.64% on 9/30 — a session when SPY fell 0.21% — alongside crude (USO +1.61%). Closing a confirmed winner on a stop technicality will look wrong if refining margins keep expanding, and it may well be wrong on the trade. It is right on the process, and the process is what the first month of stop-outs was lost to.
counter_argument: The strongest case against closing is that 1.86 ATR versus a 2.0 ATR floor is a rounding error, not a defect, and that DINO is flat rather than underwater so there is no damage to stop — enforcing the floor to the second decimal on a working position is pedantry. The answer is that the floor was set at 2.0 precisely because every one of this report first ten stop-outs came in under 1.6 ATR and the discretion to call 1.86 close enough is the discretion that produced them; and more concretely, the gap is not a rounding error once the target is checked, because 128.00 is above the 150-day high of 118.39, so the honest ratio is worse than 1.95, not better. The disciplined route is to close and re-enter with levels that clear on their own.

evidence.detail: Fetched ATR14 5.2507 (4.89% of price); the 97.75 stop is 9.75 from the 107.50 entry = 1.86 ATR, below the 2.0 stock floor. Close 107.32, SMA20 108.4555, SMA50 98.4476, 150-day range 47.00-118.39 — the 128.00 target is above the range high

The rounding-error objection is answered by recomputing at an honest 2.0 ATR stop of 97.00: reward-to-risk falls to 20.50/10.50 = 1.95, failing the 2.0 floor, and the 128.00 target used in that calculation is itself above the fetched 150-day high of 118.39

thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open GDX position (opened 2026-09-26 at 91.20, now 87.80, -3.7%) and the recommendation is a reluctant hold-unchanged. The stop at 85.40 is 5.80 from entry against a fetched ATR14 of 3.1711, which is 1.83 ATR — it clears the 1.8 ATR ETF floor, but only barely, and it is the thinnest pass in the book. Reward-to-risk from entry is (104.40-91.20)/(91.20-85.40) = 2.28, which clears the 2.0 swing floor. What keeps it rather than closing it is that the stop does clear the floor on its own arithmetic, unlike SNX at 1.38 ATR and DINO at 1.86 ATR, and the position is only two days old.
counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that the underlying has broken down and the position has not yet caught up to that fact: GLD fell 0.54% on 9/30 to 380.84 and GDX closed at 87.80, now below its SMA50 (90.98) as well as its SMA20 (94.88), where two days ago it was above the 50d. A miner ETF below both averages with the metal falling is a leveraged long on a broken trend. It is answered only weakly — the honest answer is that the 85.40 stop is 0.76 ATR below the current price and will execute within days if the breakdown continues, so the risk is bounded and short-dated rather than that the breakdown is not happening. That is a reason not to panic, not a reason for confidence, and it is why conviction stays at 3 with an explicit no-add.
key_risk: GDX has now been recommended on three separate days (twice in the last ten per prior context, plus today), which prior context flags as an anchoring warning rather than a conviction signal, and the position has gone against me on every one of them. The specific risk is that a gold position is implicitly a bet the long end stops rising, which directly contradicts the XLU short and the three awaiting duration shorts that are the best-evidenced view in this report — if the 10-year keeps climbing from 5.26%, real yields rise and gold miners are the wrong place to be. The position only survives today on stop arithmetic; it is the first thing to cut tomorrow.

thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open EEM position (opened 2026-08-21 at 65.60, now 66.79, +1.8%) and the recommendation is hold-unchanged. With PFE, it is one of only two longs of fourteen that is both profitable and above its 50d SMA (66.31), against eleven that sit below both their 20d and 50d averages. The stop at 63.00 is 2.60 from entry against a fetched ATR14 of 1.1065, so 2.35 ATR against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor, and reward-to-risk from entry is (71.50-65.60)/(65.60-63.00) = 2.27. EEM is 6.68% off its 150-day high of 71.57 and 22.7% above its low of 54.435, so the trend structure is intact rather than merely unbroken.
key_risk: EEM fell 0.91% on 9/30 and closed at 66.79, just below its SMA20 of 67.46, so the short-term trend has rolled even though the 50d holds — the position is at an inflection rather than in clear air. The structural risk is the dollar: UUP closed at 28.77 and rose 0.07% on 9/30, and with the US 10-year at 5.26% the carry argument favours the dollar, which is the standard mechanism by which emerging-market equity returns are taken away. I did not fetch a dollar-index level beyond the UUP ETF proxy, since the macro DXY call failed, so the currency leg of this thesis is read through a proxy rather than measured directly.
counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that a 5.26% US 10-year is historically the condition emerging markets underperform in, because dollar funding gets expensive and capital repatriates — so the same macro read that makes the XLU short the best idea in the book should logically make EEM a short, not a long. The answer is that the mechanism requires the dollar to actually rise and it has not: UUP is flat at 28.77 (+0.07% on 9/30), and EEM has absorbed the entire move in the 10-year while staying 22.7% above its 150-day low and above its 50d SMA. A thesis whose transmission channel is not transmitting is not yet a reason to close a working position — but it is a reason not to add, and it is why this is conviction 3.

evidence.detail: Fetched ATR14 1.1065; the 63.00 stop is 2.60 from the 65.60 entry = 2.35 ATR against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor. Close 66.79 above SMA50 66.3084, marginally below SMA20 67.457, 150-day range 54.435-71.57

The dollar-funding objection is answered by measuring the transmission channel: UUP closed 28.77, +0.07% on 9/30 and flat on the week, so the dollar has not risen on the 10-year move to 5.26% and the EM-drain mechanism is not engaged

thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open SVRA position (opened 2026-08-23 at 5.35, now 5.16, -3.6%) and the recommendation is hold-unchanged at 1% lottery-ticket size. It survives on risk bounding rather than on fresh evidence: the 4.60 stop is 0.75 from entry against a fetched ATR14 of 0.2284, so 3.28 ATR — the second-widest in the book relative to the 2.0 ATR floor — and reward-to-risk from entry is (8.00-5.35)/(5.35-4.60) = 3.53. Liquidity clears the universe floor with room: fetched 30-day average dollar volume is 9.69M USD per day against the 500K USD minimum, so a 1% position is a small fraction of daily turnover and is exitable.
key_risk: This is a conviction 2 and its thinness is the main risk, stated plainly: I verified NO dated catalyst for SVRA inside the swing horizon — it appears in no date of the fetched 12-session earnings calendar and I did not reach its filings inside this run budget — so the only evidence under it is a price level and a liquidity measurement. As a sub-$6 clinical-stage biotech it carries the two risks that kill these theses before the science is settled: a secondary offering diluting the equity, which is the single most common outcome for a company at this size funding trials, and a trading halt on a data release that cannot be exited through. It is also below both its SMA20 (5.27) and SMA50 (5.41), so the trend is against it. Size is what makes it publishable — at 1% a total loss costs 1%; the same idea at 5% would not be.
counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that it is a thesis with no catalyst I could date and no primary document I read, in a name 20.3% off its 150-day high and below both moving averages — which is indistinguishable from the falling knives being closed today in LCII and LULU. The honest answer is that the distinction is bounded risk and size, not better evidence: SVRA has a 3.28 ATR working stop and is held at 1%, whereas LCII and LULU carry no stop at all and were sized as real positions. That answers why it is not closed; it does not answer why it would be bought today, and it would not be.
